title: Junior IT Support Technician
description: Banks, fintechs, and BPO firms across Accra (including Stanbic, Hubtel, and MTN Ghana) hire entry-level IT support technicians to handle helpdesk tickets, install hardware, and maintain office networks. Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) lists IT services as a priority growth sector.

title: Mining Safety Officer
description: Major gold mining operators in Tarkwa, Obuasi and Ahafo (Newmont, Gold Fields, AngloGold Ashanti) recruit safety officers with an HND in mining, geology or occupational health to enforce site safety standards under Minerals Commission regulations. Strong demand but credentialed entry only.

title: Financial Services Customer Agent
description: Tier-2 banks, savings & loans companies and microfinance institutions across Accra and Kumasi recruit customer agents to manage account opening, KYC capture, and basic transaction support. Bank of Ghana licensing rules require WASSCE-minimum candidates and English fluency.

title: Furniture Export Coordinator
description: Kumasi's Sokoban Wood Village and Anloga workshops produce hardwood furniture exported to Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire and Europe. A coordinator with carpentry experience and basic export documentation skills can earn 1,800–3,500 GHS monthly liaising between artisan workshops, GIPC export desks, and overseas buyers. KNUST Department of Wood Science offers short courses on export-grade finishing.

title: Solar PV Installer
description: Off-grid solar demand is growing in Northern Ghana and peri-urban Greater Accra. Independent installers certified through COTVET (Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training) earn 1,500–3,000 GHS per installation. Energy Commission of Ghana maintains a registered installer list.

title: MTN Mobile Money Agent
description: MTN Mobile Money and Vodafone Cash sub-agent networks let youth operate kiosks earning commissions on deposits, withdrawals and bill payments. Float capital of around 2,000 GHS is required. Mobile money penetration in Ghana exceeds 60% of adults (Bank of Ghana 2024).

title: Bolt / Uber Driver
description: Ride-hailing platforms Bolt and Uber operate at scale in Accra and Kumasi. A driver with a DVLA-licensed vehicle (own or rented) clears 600–1,500 GHS monthly after fuel and platform commission. Income peaks during weekends and rainy season.

title: Freelance Graphic Designer
description: SMEs, churches, and event organisers across Ghana commission freelance designers for flyers, social media graphics and logos via WhatsApp and Instagram. Self-taught designers using Canva or Adobe Express can earn 400–2,500 GHS monthly depending on client portfolio.

title: KNUST Wood Science Short Course
description: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science & Technology (KNUST) Department of Wood Science and Technology offers 8-12 week short courses on export-grade finishing, kiln drying and product certification — directly applicable for carpentry apprentices targeting the regional furniture export market via GIPC trade desks.

title: MEST Africa Entrepreneurship Fellowship
description: Meltwater Entrepreneurial School of Technology (MEST Africa) in East Legon, Accra runs a fully-funded 12-month fellowship covering software engineering, product management and entrepreneurship for African graduates. Selective intake; accepts strong portfolios in lieu of formal CS degree.
